---
title: Add a Theme to a Kickstart
description: Learn how to use Kickstart to create a FusionAuth Instance with a custom theme.
tags: kickstart, custom theme, theme automation, docker setup, theme deployment, freemarker, login page customization, branding
---

[[Kickstart]] configures a new FusionAuth instance from a template file on first startup. In this guide, you write a Kickstart that replaces the default theme with a dark theme. The Kickstart also creates the following:

* An Application named `Kickstart App` with OAuth settings.
* A user who can log in to the Admin UI and who has a Registration for the Kickstart App.

[First Time Setup](/docs/get-started/first-time-setup) creates the same Application and user by hand. You don't need to complete First Time Setup before this guide.

## Prerequisites

You need Docker. For the Docker requirements, see [Install Locally](/docs/get-started/install#prerequisites).

## The Default Theme

FusionAuth uses the default theme until you assign a different theme. The OAuth authorize page in the default theme looks like this:

<Screenshot id="theme-preview-oauth-authorize" url="/admin/theme/view/75a068fd-e94b-451a-9aeb-3ddb9a3b5987#oauth2Authorize" height={1100} alt="The OAuth authorize page in the default FusionAuth theme." />

The OAuth logout page in the default theme looks like this:

<Screenshot id="theme-preview-oauth-logout" url="/admin/theme/view/75a068fd-e94b-451a-9aeb-3ddb9a3b5987#oauth2Logout" height={1100} alt="The OAuth logout page in the default FusionAuth theme.">
  <Highlight selector="main button[data-tab='oauth2Logout']" />
</Screenshot>

After you finish this guide, the same pages look like this:

![The OAuth authorize page in the dark theme.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/preview-authorize-dark.png)

![The OAuth logout page in the dark theme.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/preview-logout-dark.png)

## Create the Kickstart Files

The Kickstart needs the following files:

* `darkTheme.css`, a stylesheet that defines the dark theme.
* `kickstart.json`, which lists the variables, the API key, and the API requests that configure FusionAuth.
* One JSON file for each API request.

To skip writing the files, download the [`theme-css-only` example](https://github.com/FusionAuth/fusionauth-example-kickstart/tree/main/theme-css-only) and go to [Download the Docker Compose File](#download-the-docker-compose-file).

### Write the Stylesheet

A stylesheet restyles every page in a theme. Write the CSS rules with the web inspector of your browser:

1. In the Admin UI, navigate to <Breadcrumb>Customizations -> Themes</Breadcrumb> and click <IconButton icon="view" /> on the row for `FusionAuth`.
1. Right-click the page and select <Breadcrumb>Inspect</Breadcrumb>.
1. Click <Breadcrumb>Select element</Breadcrumb>, then click the area of the page to style. For example, click the `div` element with the class `.panel`.

   ![The web inspector with the panel element selected.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/div-panel-bg.png)

   The `.panel` element has a **`background`** of `#fff`, which is white.

1. With the element selected, click <Breadcrumb>+</Breadcrumb> and type `background: black`.

   ![The web inspector with a new background rule on the panel element.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/background-black.png)

1. Copy the rule, including the selector the browser added, into a file named `darkTheme.css`:

   ```css
   .panel {
     background: black
   }
   ```

Repeat the process for each element to restyle. For a complete dark theme, use the [`darkTheme.css` example file](https://github.com/FusionAuth/fusionauth-example-kickstart/blob/main/theme-css-only/darkTheme.css).

Create a folder named `kickstart`, and move `darkTheme.css` into the folder.

### Write `kickstart.json`

`kickstart.json` configures FusionAuth on first startup. Create `kickstart/kickstart.json` with the following contents:

```json
{
  "variables":{
    "apiKey" : "#{UUID()}",
    "themeID" : "#{UUID()}",
    "applicationID" : "404e516b-06b8-49da-9c68-c1cd1928c81d",
    "clientSecret" : "RBLhJrfRsa0-YxVPrn_aZfzIGccWyncdvHvDNTy-Hrs",
    "defaultTenantId": "da025934-3ba7-4a13-83f0-aab68c9919b8",
    "userID" : "#{UUID()}"
  },
  "apiKeys": [
    {
      "key": "#{apiKey}"
    }
  ],
  "requests":[
    "&{json/createTheme.json}",
    "&{json/updateTheme.json}",
    "&{json/createApplication.json}",
    "&{json/createUser.json}",
    "&{json/registerUser.json}",
    "&{json/setDefaultTheme.json}"
  ]
}
```

The file has three sections:

* **`variables`** defines values that the requests reuse. **`apiKey`**, **`themeID`**, and **`userID`** get random UUIDs. **`applicationID`**, **`clientSecret`**, and **`defaultTenantId`** have fixed values, so you know the values in advance. **`defaultTenantId`** sets the Id of the [[default tenant]].
* **`apiKeys`** defines the API key that Kickstart uses to run the requests. Every `kickstart.json` needs at least one API key.
* **`requests`** lists the API requests in the order Kickstart runs them. Each `&{...}` entry loads a request from a separate file. A request can also live inline in `kickstart.json`, but separate files are easier to edit when a Kickstart grows.

### Write the API Requests

Create a folder named `json` inside the `kickstart` folder. Add each of the following files to the `json` folder.

`createTheme.json` creates the dark theme:

```json
{
  "method" : "POST",
  "url" : "api/theme/#{themeID}",
  "body" : {
    "sourceThemeId" : "75a068fd-e94b-451a-9aeb-3ddb9a3b5987",
    "theme" : {
      "name" : "Dark Theme"
    }
  }
}
```

**`sourceThemeId`** copies the default FusionAuth theme, which always has the Id `75a068fd-e94b-451a-9aeb-3ddb9a3b5987`. The URL path sets the Id of the new theme to the **`themeID`** variable.

`updateTheme.json` applies `darkTheme.css` to the new theme:

```json
{
  "method" : "PATCH",
  "url" : "api/theme/#{themeID}",
  "body" : {
    "theme" : {
      "stylesheet" : "@{darkTheme.css}"
    }
  }
}
```

`setDefaultTheme.json` assigns the dark theme to the default tenant:

```json
{
  "method": "PATCH",
  "url": "/api/tenant/#{defaultTenantId}",
  "body": {
    "tenant": {
      "themeId": "#{themeID}"
    }
  }
}
```

`createApplication.json` creates the Kickstart App:

```json
{
  "method" : "POST",
  "url" : "/api/application/#{applicationID}",
  "body" : {
    "application":{
      "name" : "Kickstart App",
      "oauthConfiguration" : {
        "authorizedRedirectURLs" : [
          "http://localhost:3000/oauth-redirect"
        ],
        "clientId" : "#{applicationID}",
        "clientSecret" : "#{clientSecret}",
        "logoutURL": "http://localhost:3000/logout",
        "enabledGrants": [
          "authorization_code",
          "refresh_token"
        ],
        "requireRegistration" : "true"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The Kickstart App uses the same OAuth settings that First Time Setup uses. The redirect URL and logout URL point to an app on port `3000`. This guide doesn't run that app. FusionAuth checks the **`redirect_uri`** of an authorize request against **`authorizedRedirectURLs`**, so the Application still needs a redirect URL to show the login page.

`createUser.json` creates a user with a Registration for the FusionAuth application, so the user can log in to the Admin UI:

```json
{
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "/api/user/registration/#{userID}",
  "body": {
    "user": {
      "email": "richard@example.com",
      "password": "password"
    },
    "registration": {
      "applicationId": "#{FUSIONAUTH_APPLICATION_ID}",
      "roles": [
        "admin"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

`registerUser.json` adds a second Registration for the Kickstart App:

```json
{
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "/api/user/registration/#{userID}",
  "body": {
    "registration": {
      "applicationId": "#{applicationID}"
    }
  }
}
```

The second Registration needs a separate request, because `createUser.json` uses the **`registration`** field for the FusionAuth application.

## Download the Docker Compose File

The FusionAuth `docker-compose.yml` mounts a `kickstart` folder next to the file and runs `kickstart/kickstart.json` on first startup. In the folder that holds your `kickstart` folder, download the file:

```shell-session
curl -o docker-compose.yml https://fusionauth.io/docs/docker-compose.yml
```

When another FusionAuth instance runs on port `9011`, stop that instance first. Run `docker compose down` in the folder of that instance.

For other ways to run Kickstart in Docker, see [Docker Configuration](/docs/deploy/production/install/docker-configuration#kickstart).

## Run Kickstart

Your folder should now look like the following. This guide calls the folder `Kickstart_Theme`, but any name works.

```
+ Kickstart_Theme
|
+-- docker-compose.yml
|
+--+ kickstart
   |
   +-- kickstart.json
   |
   +-- darkTheme.css
   |
   +--+ json
      |
      +-- createTheme.json
      |
      +-- updateTheme.json
      |
      +-- createUser.json
      |
      +-- registerUser.json
      |
      +-- createApplication.json
      |
      +-- setDefaultTheme.json
```

To launch the FusionAuth instance, run the following command in the `Kickstart_Theme` folder:

```shell-session
docker compose up
```

After Kickstart finishes, FusionAuth runs at `http://localhost:9011`.

Log in to the Admin UI at `http://localhost:9011/admin`. `kickstart/json/createUser.json` sets the email and password. This guide uses the following values:

```json
"email": "richard@example.com",
"password": "password"
```

To confirm that Kickstart configured everything, look at <Breadcrumb>Applications</Breadcrumb>, <Breadcrumb>Users</Breadcrumb>, and <Breadcrumb>Customizations -> Themes</Breadcrumb>.

## View the Themed Pages

To preview the dark theme, navigate to <Breadcrumb>Customizations -> Themes</Breadcrumb>. Click <IconButton icon="view" /> on the row for `Dark Theme`. The preview renders every themed page, including the OAuth authorize and OAuth logout pages.

To see the live login page, open the following URL in a private browser window:

```plaintext
http://localhost:9011/oauth2/authorize?client_id=404e516b-06b8-49da-9c68-c1cd1928c81d&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Foauth-redirect&response_type=code
```

The private window keeps your Admin UI session from logging you in. FusionAuth shows the login page with the dark theme:

![The login page with the dark theme applied.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/dark-authorize.png)

Close the window without logging in. A login redirects the browser to `localhost:3000`, and no app runs there.

## Change a Default Message

A Kickstart can also change the text on themed pages. The following steps change the "Forgot your password?" link on the OAuth authorize page to "Forgot your password? Click here."

![The Forgot your password link on the login page.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/forgot-password.png)

The **`defaultMessages`** field of a theme replaces every message at once. The value must contain every message in the default messages file that ships with FusionAuth. To get the full set:

1. In the Admin UI, edit the dark theme.
1. Click <Breadcrumb>Messages</Breadcrumb>, then click <Breadcrumb>Edit</Breadcrumb>.

   <Screenshot id="theme-dark-messages" url="/admin/theme/edit/9c2d4e6f-8a1b-4c3d-9e5f-7a6b5c4d3e21" alt="The default messages of the dark theme, with the forgot-your-password message highlighted.">
     <Highlight selector="[data-hl='forgot-message']" />
   </Screenshot>

1. Copy every message into a new file, `kickstart/defaultMessages.txt`.
1. In `defaultMessages.txt`, change the value of `forgot-your-password` to `Forgot your password? Click here.`

Add **`defaultMessages`** to `json/updateTheme.json`:

```json
{
  "method" : "PATCH",
  "url" : "api/theme/#{themeID}",
  "body" : {
    "theme" : {
      "stylesheet" : "@{darkTheme.css}",
      "defaultMessages" : "@{defaultMessages.txt}"
    }
  }
}
```

Kickstart runs only on an empty database. When FusionAuth finds any users, API keys, or Applications, FusionAuth skips the Kickstart to protect the data. To run the updated Kickstart, delete the Docker volumes of the instance:

<Aside type="danger">
`docker compose down -v` deletes every user, Application, and setting in the instance.
</Aside>

```shell-session
docker compose down -v
```

Then start the instance again:

```shell-session
docker compose up
```

The login page now shows the new message:

![The login page with the updated Forgot your password message.](/img/docs/customize/look-and-feel/updated-message.png)

For more ways to customize a theme, see [Themes](/docs/theme). To manage themes with the API, see the [Themes API](/docs/apis/themes).
